mainTopic: Two שותפין (partners) who made a נדר forbidding הנאה from each other, and whether they may still use the חצר they share
overview: This amud opens a new משנה about two שותפין (partners) who made a נדר forbidding any הנאה from each other. The question is whether they may still use the חצר they own together. The תנא קמא says neither may enter, because the courtyard is shared and each partner would be using the other's share. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב disagrees. He says each partner is seen as walking only on his own portion, so he gets no הנאה from his partner. Their argument comes down to how to view shared property: as belonging to both partners at every point, or as divided into separate shares.

steps.title: Partners who forbade benefit from each other may not enter their shared courtyard
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא rules that שותפין who made a נדר against הנאה from each other are forbidden to enter their jointly owned חצר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Partners who vowed not to get any benefit from one another are forbidden to enter the courtyard they share.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens with a case: two partners own a חצר together, and each makes a נדר not to benefit from the other. The first opinion says neither of them may go into the courtyard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two partners own the courtyard together, so every part of it belongs a little to each of them. When one partner walks in, he is also using the other partner's share. That counts as forbidden הנאה.

keyTerms.meaning: Benefit; getting any use or enjoyment from something
From one another (each from the other)

steps.confusionAlert: Each partner did not forbid himself from his own property. He only forbade benefit from his partner. The problem comes from the courtyard being shared: when he uses his own part, he is also using his partner's part.

phrases.english: not to benefit from one another
phrases.notes: The word 'not' isn't written. A vow about הנאה means he is forbidding himself from benefiting.

phrases.english: are forbidden to enter the courtyard
phrases.notes: This is the courtyard the two of them own together.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the משנה with a new case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Partners who forbade הנאה from each other may not enter their shared חצר, because each would be using the other's share.

steps.title: Each partner is seen as entering only his own share
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב disagrees and permits both partners to enter. Each one is viewed as walking only on his own portion of the חצר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says: this one is entering his own part, and that one is entering his own part.
steps.whatsHappening: A second תנא argues with the first opinion. He says both partners may use the courtyard, because each is considered to be on his own share.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא saw every inch of the courtyard as belonging to both partners together. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב looks at it differently: each partner is treated as using only the part that is his. If he is only on his own part, he gets no הנאה from his partner, so the נדר is not broken.

keyTerms.meaning: A תַּנָּא who disagrees with the first opinion here

steps.whatToRemember: The argument in this משנה is about how to view shared property. The תנא קמא sees it as belonging to both partners at every point, so entering is forbidden. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב sees each partner as using only his own share, so entering is allowed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This argument shapes how the גמרא will understand shared ownership whenever there is a נדר against הנאה between partners.

phrases.english: this one enters into his own
phrases.notes: 'His own' means his own share of the courtyard.

phrases.english: and that one enters into his own

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a disagreeing opinion to the ruling in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both partners may enter the shared חצר, since each is seen as using only his own portion.
